summary: ING sits clearly with the traditional banks (position score 0.257), and its measured signature is the densest urgency and deadline language in the set - 4.0 markers per page against a peer mean of 0.64, about 3.7 standard deviations from the market, the largest gap in the set - combined with above-peer offer clarity and fast digital sign-up claims. Calls to action are withheld rather than reported: ING's pack cards render client-side and are absent from the captured HTML, so any count would measure the capture and not the page. These are design observations only: the pages span several product families and languages, the judged features come from a single rater, and no click or conversion data exists, so every item below is a hypothesis ING could test.

recommendations.title: Strip back urgency and deadline language
recommendations.finding: Urgency and deadline language is ING's largest measured gap: 4.0 markers per page against a peer mean of 0.64, roughly 3.7 standard deviations above the peer set, and it is also the strongest element of ING's market signature at about 2.5 standard deviations.
recommendations.recommendation: Remove countdown and deadline phrasing from current-account and account-opening copy, and replace it with a plain statement of what the offer includes and how long it is contractually valid, if at all.

recommendations.title: Disclose the conditions of any free claim next to the claim
recommendations.finding: The 'free' with conditions attached measure is 0.67 for ING against a peer mean of 0.23, the largest qualitative gap after urgency and persuasion. Where a free or no-fee claim appears, the qualifying conditions are not adjacent to it on the same page.
recommendations.recommendation: Place the qualifying conditions of every free or no-fee claim directly beneath the claim, in the same block and at readable size, instead of leaving them to the page's legal small print.

recommendations.title: Shorten the pages and cut non-informative imagery
recommendations.finding: Page length is 11148.67 pixels against a peer mean of 6411.72, about 1.4 standard deviations above, and pages carry 33 images against a peer mean of 19. Long, question-heavy pages are a trait of the traditional cluster generally (around 20.7 questions against 5.75 at challengers), so length is not unique to ING, but ING is at the long end.
recommendations.recommendation: Merge or cut the lower sections of the current-account pages so the offer, its conditions and the call to action fit within fewer screens, and remove images that do not carry information the reader needs in order to decide.

recommendations.title: Reduce the number of persuasion techniques stacked per page
recommendations.finding: Persuasion techniques used measures 3.67 for ING against a peer mean of 1.74, about 2.5 standard deviations above peers. Combined with the urgency finding, ING's pages apply the densest persuasion in the comparison set.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep one persuasion device per section - a benefit statement, a proof point or a reassurance - and delete the overlapping ones so the offer itself carries the argument rather than the framing around it.

recommendations.title: Anchor the repeated calls to action on the existing clear offer statement
recommendations.finding: Clarity of the offer is a genuine ING strength at 5.0 against a peer mean of 3.74, about 1.5 standard deviations above, and it is one of the three features in ING's market signature at 1.3 standard deviations. Makes the offer feel worth having is also above peers at 1.0 against 0.59.
recommendations.recommendation: Restate the offer in one sentence immediately above each repeated call to action, so the clearest and most desirable part of the page is what the reader sees at the moment of acting.

recommendations.title: Substantiate the fast digital sign-up claim or drop it
recommendations.finding: Promises fast digital sign-up is 0.67 for ING against a peer mean of 0.15, about 1.4 standard deviations above, and it forms part of ING's market signature at 1.3 standard deviations. Subscription style framing, by contrast, is a challenger trait (0.5 against 0.0 for traditional banks), not something ING currently uses.
recommendations.recommendation: Attach checkable detail to the fast digital sign-up claim - how many steps it takes and what the customer must have at hand - or remove the claim from pages where the opening journey is longer than the copy implies. Borrowing the challengers' plain subscription framing is one way to do this without new claims.

recommendations.title: Use contrast rather than more brightness to single out the action
recommendations.finding: Page brightness is 0.55 for ING against a peer mean of 0.34, and brightness is already a traditional-bank trait (0.43 against 0.17 at challengers, a large effect). ING is brighter than its own cluster, so additional brightness is unlikely to differentiate it.
recommendations.recommendation: Hold the current background brightness and instead make the single primary call to action the darkest or most saturated element in its section, so contrast does the work of directing the eye.

recommendations.title: Keep digital claims concrete while ING's own news themes are silent on digital
recommendations.finding: In the last 90 days ING has 2 headlines, both themed 'other' (a JPMorgan favourite-list item and a shared piece on daily transfer limits), and nothing under innovation_digital. BNP Paribas Fortis shows 1 headline under innovation_digital and Revolut 1. If ING's pages lean on digital-leadership framing, the current press picture does not corroborate it; this link is a hypothesis to verify, not evidence about page performance.
recommendations.recommendation: On pages describing digital account opening or digital banking, prefer concrete, checkable statements - number of steps, documents needed, timing - over leadership or 'best digital bank' style framing until there is coverage outside ING that supports it.
recommendations.reputation_context: Based on ING's 90-day theme counts (2 headlines, both 'other') and the innovation_digital theme appearing once each for BNP Paribas Fortis and Revolut.

recommendations.title: Avoid time pressure on pages that describe account access and limits
recommendations.finding: One of ING's two 90-day headlines is a shared article on daily transfer limits capped at 5,000 EUR, running alongside Belfius, BNP Paribas Fortis and Crelan. Attention is currently on what a current account does and does not allow, so 'act now' framing placed near account-access copy risks being read against that topic. This is a hypothesis to verify, not a measured page effect.
recommendations.recommendation: On current-account and account-opening pages, keep the copy focused on what the account includes rather than on time pressure, and state any limit or access condition explicitly in the section where the account is described.
recommendations.reputation_context: Drawn from ING's 2 headlines in the 90-day window, one of which is the shared daily-transfer-limit story also involving Belfius, BNP Paribas Fortis and Crelan.

recommendations.title: Place data and payment protection beside the account-opening action
recommendations.finding: Belfius carries 9 crisis_or_scandal headlines in the 90-day window, including a criminal case over an unindemnified phishing victim, and Revolut carries 1, a data-sharing incident after a fraudulent request. ING shows no crisis_or_scandal theme of its own in that window. Trust and data handling are therefore live topics for Belgian banking readers; whether that changes behaviour on a page is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: Add a short factual statement on how customer data and payments are protected, positioned directly next to the account-opening call to action rather than as a generic badge further down the page.
recommendations.reputation_context: Drawn from crisis_or_scandal theme counts in the 90-day window: Belfius 9, Revolut 1, ING 0.
